brief: A short explainer on how a heat pump pulls heat out of cold outdoor air, for homeowners thinking about getting one. Calm, plain words.

scenes.narration: Even on a freezing morning, the air outside still holds heat.
scenes.visual: A frosted back garden at dawn, a heat pump unit against a brick wall, its fan turning slowly, slow push-in.

sentences.text: Even on a freezing morning, the air outside still holds heat.

scenes.narration: A heat pump gathers it with a refrigerant that runs colder than the air itself.
scenes.visual: Close-up of frosted copper coils and aluminium fins on the outdoor unit, vapour drifting past.

sentences.text: A heat pump gathers it with a refrigerant that runs colder than the air itself.

scenes.narration: A compressor squeezes the refrigerant, and squeezing a gas makes it hot.
scenes.visual: A clean studio shot of a compressor in a cutaway housing, a warm orange glow building inside it.

sentences.text: A compressor squeezes the refrigerant, and squeezing a gas makes it hot.

scenes.narration: Indoors, that heat passes into the air, or into the water in your radiators.
scenes.visual: A warm living room in late-afternoon light, a radiator under the window, steam rising from a mug on the sill.

sentences.text: Indoors, that heat passes into the air, or into the water in your radiators.

scenes.narration: Then the refrigerant cools, expands, and goes back outside to start again.
scenes.visual: Blue liquid flowing through a loop of pipes, from a warm room back out to a frosty garden, smooth tracking shot.

sentences.text: Then the refrigerant cools, expands, and goes back outside to start again.

scenes.narration: It moves heat rather than making it, which is why it needs so little electricity.
scenes.visual: A kitchen wall display showing a quiet energy readout as a family walks past, soft natural light.

sentences.text: It moves heat rather than making it, which is why it needs so little electricity.

title: How a heat pump works
